name: Sticker Cast
summary: A die-cut sticker world where a one-eyed teal Pulse sticker spots the anomaly and an emoji cast reacts from tired to shocked to happy.
look: Mint dotted backdrop, everything a vinyl sticker with a fat white border and soft shadow; emoji-style amber faces, chart stickers and die-cut lettering.

components.name: Die-cut sticker
components.role: any element with a fat white border and soft drop shadow

components.name: Pulse eye
components.role: teal one-eyed sticker creature with the coral dot; the watcher

components.name: Emoji reactions
components.role: tired → shocked → happy faces carry the emotional beat

components.name: Chart stickers
components.role: mini dashboards, overlapping and rotated = overload

components.name: Die-cut lettering
components.role: headlines with a thick white stroke outline

components.name: Sticker sheet
components.role: backing paper with kiss-cut outlines for the CTA

motion.name: Slap-on
motion.how: scale 1.25→1 with rotation settle, 0.12 s expo.out + 0.2 s elastic wobble; every slap sits on an 8th or quarter note

motion.name: Peel & re-stick
motion.how: corner curl via a rotating triangle mask, 0.3 s power2.inOut, released on the backbeat

motion.name: Eye dart
motion.how: Pulse’s iris snaps to its target in 0.08 s power4.out, 1 beat before the thing it looks at reacts

story: Hook: a pile of 38 dashboard stickers and a tired face under 'How many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: the Acme mark sticker slams down with 'Acme Pulse' lettering and the Pulse eye. Proof: an anomaly card sticker (checkout −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231), a shocked face, and a hand sticker pressing Roll back. CTA: a sticker sheet with 'Every metric. Every minute.' and a Start free sticker.
adapt: Die-cut your own UI cards, logo and one mascot as stickers, pick 3 emoji-style reactions for your before/during/after, and make your CTA the last sticker on the sheet.

references.note: open-source (MIT) emoji faces for flat/3D reaction styles
Lottie-based animated stickers at 60 fps: the motion language of chat

fit.risk: Can tip into ‘meme’ and undercut trust — keep one real data card crisp and unrotated enough to read, and limit the cast to 3 characters.
